; Initialize the intro palette selection and dispatch on scene_state. The cold path seeds option, season and progress fields and clears the saved continuation flags before loading the first display. Later paths select results, practice, ending or the next menu scene; scene dispatch does not return in this bank context.

; Load the audio descriptor, clear scene work and initialize the scrolling intro. The local continuation now includes the later display/raster effects; the two ambiguous intro bytes remain a separate raw interval.
; While no controller transition is pending, present the next intro display; resume the shared input/scene continuation afterward.
; If no controller input is held, enter the intro continuation; otherwise skip toward the next accepted block.
; With no input transition, decrement scene_state; a negative result leaves the sequence while nonnegative values return to the preceding display wait.
; Clear the scene flag and wait for button release before the next scene transition.

; Reset display/audio before leaving the intro. Dispatch by scene state and the season/practice continuation flags; completed races show sorted results and update the next track state. The season sign and low bits select the ordinary, special or ending path.

; Build eight four-byte sprite records, load palette and compressed nametable, then accelerate a fixed-point scroll. The high scroll accumulator terminates the first sweep; the delay permits an input escape.

; Wait through the installed intro callback, snapshot eight OAM positions into word accumulators, and apply eight signed velocity pairs for thirty frames. Then walk the animation source in 66-byte steps until the stop flag or input abort. The nested stream worker may discard its caller return on abort; the ordinary return still reaches the source advance.
; Add the fractional velocity to a scroll step, update the screen once per frame and accumulate distance. A button press discards this routine's return address to exit its caller early.
; Increase the shared Y position by four until $90 and copy it into all eight OAM records. The exact stop value prevents further movement.
; Eight initial Y coordinates followed by encoded text and counted sprite backing. Intro sprite/stream consumers use this neighborhood; exact internal object subjects remain uncertain.
; Reset display, select palette values and load the secondary intro nametable and sprite resources. Install the raster callback and finish with a bounded input-sensitive wait.

; Mixed intro display backing: ordered tile values, repeated record fields and palette-like groups. Nearby display loaders and immutable bytes were checked; keep the mixed extent as data without inventing individual resource endpoints.
; Continue into the second intro display and its raster effects.

; Finish both animation stages unless input intervenes. Count a sixteen-bit hold interval while button mask $08 remains held, then match eight subsequent input transitions against the local sequence. A complete match opens the alternate display; any mismatch returns.
; Eight controller masks checked in order after the initial held-button interval. Each new transition must match the next byte; a mismatch abandons the alternate intro path.

; Load the second intro display and install the moving composite callback. Its fixed-point X position decreases by two per frame; the Y byte rises by two. The following raster chain selects scanlines and scrolls bands until the controller advances it.
; Install the idle callback and draw the fixed intro text at its supplied origin before returning.
; Select the intro panel source and queue its rectangle with attribute data at the fixed origin.
; Two six-byte prefixes drive the raster hooks with index limited to 0..5; two trailing numeric bytes are retained without assuming another full table.
; Count byte followed by sixteen four-byte sprite records. The intro callback supplies the source and screen origin to the shared composite renderer.

; Encoded name/text corpus followed by small repeated tile/palette fields. Nearby intro consumers and neighboring strings support display backing; exact mixed-object endpoints are not all established.

Initialize display, text, sprites and relative animation frames; later frame waits and controller checks advance the sequence. ; Initialize sixteen driver indices and sort their two-plane result words in descending order using adjacent swaps until a pass makes no changes. Save the leading result, load the mode-specific display and render all sixteen names and result fields. Mode zero draws rank awards; the alternate mode draws converted result quantities.
; Choose the alternate result-display mode before joining the shared sixteen-row result renderer.
; Single tile$D6queued with explicit count1by the result-row renderer. This byte is not an executable continuation.

; For each sorted driver, display a special text for negative result words or split a nonnegative result into three base60 fields. Render those fields and advance the row and wrapped driver index. After16rows install the results callback, save the selected driver and wait for input.
; Every twenty calls toggle bit 7 of the display state, choose ROM text or RAM text, and queue a sixteen-tile strip. The initial jump is a separate release-wait entry.
; Short encoded label followed by sixteen blank tiles for the player-name row. The result renderer selects player storage separately from the fixed driver-name pointers.

; Scale the supplied three-byte result through the selected multiplier and divide helper, round the low discarded bit upward, and render the resulting numeric field. The neighboring formatting entry splits the leading result into three base60 pieces; the final helper maps a 0..59 remainder through quotient/remainder-by-six lookup bytes. Exact physical units remain uncertain.
; Split the leading three-byte result into three base60remainders and draw the formatted fields at their mode-dependent positions.
; Preserve X and repeatedly subtract6from Y to obtain two finite indices. Combine the two correction planes and restore X; input remainder is bounded below 60 by its caller.
; Ten multiples of 10 followed by six low-digit corrections. The formatter repeatedly subtracts6from a base60remainder, then combines one byte from each plane; no wider input domain is implied.

; Take the 24-bit quantity in A:Y:X, divide by 60 with the shared arithmetic helpers, and subtract quotient times60 from the saved input. Return quotient in Y:X and the low remainder in A. The stack holds the quotient bytes, not a nonlocal return.

; Selector pointers, short encoded labels and counted sprite records used by the result display. Internal mixed resource subjects remain uncertain; the following physical bank continues backing without changing this boundary.

; Continuation of repeated four-byte sprite records and display backing across the physical8KiB boundary. CPU address continuity requires the accepted consecutive bank pair; this is not a new executable root.
; Set the default option, reset display, load the first intro nametable and palette, set the shared delay and enter an input-sensitive wait.
; An accepted one-byte return entry; caller-specific purpose remains unresolved.
; Encoded names and repeated display/palette patterns beside the first intro loader. Numeric prefix meaning remains unresolved; repeated noninstruction organization supports generic display backing.
; Load the alternate nametable and palette, wait for release and a bounded input interval, then reset and return to the ordinary intro continuation.
; Alternate intro display backing with ordered tile runs and repeated palette fields. Consumer adjacency and byte patterns were checked; retain mixed format uncertainty.

; Copy the 24-bit input to cartridge scratch. Repeated subtraction against five place-value planes yields encoded digits; failed subtraction pops only its two temporary bytes. Reverse the digit order with balanced stack storage, calculate a four-bit XOR/add checksum, encode it through the local alphabet and enter the result-code scene.

; Encoded result alphabet, five24-bit place-value planes and neighboring pointer/header bytes. The result encoder repeatedly subtracts each place value and adds a four-bit checksum; only those consumed subroles are claimed.
; Uniform non-code run of $00, length 33. Boundaries and pattern inspected in phase-1 evidence; no specific table format or consumer is established.

; Audio header/directory backing followed by repeated note/duration/control pairs. The local audio consumers and matching neighboring sequence structures were checked; exact song/voice subjects and the full original header schema remain uncertain.
; Uniform non-code run of $FF, length 499. Boundaries and pattern inspected in phase-1 evidence; no specific table format or consumer is established.

; Validate the three-byte saved-data signature, initialize options and blank password storage when absent, then restore saved season/selection fields. Scene state chooses the menu, continuation or score path. On race completion render awards, update accumulated scores, advance the season selector and enter the next scene.

; Convert 34 password characters through the inverse alphabet, rejecting the all-$ff sentinel and checking the low-nibble sum against character 35. Invalid input clears menu_mode_flag. The following entry applies only the fields enabled in its caller-supplied mask.
; Search the alphabet with an eight-bit index and return its inverse code. Callers supply display characters. If no byte matches, index wrap exits the loop and uses inverse entry zero.

; If validation succeeded, apply the fields selected by the mask in $44. Restore sixteen packed score words with a season-dependent offset, then optionally restore season, track and progression fields.

; Subtract the season offset from sixteen score words, pack low five bits and the remaining high bits into separate character runs, append season/track/progression fields and a four-bit checksum, then map codes back to display characters. This routine changes score scratch in cartridge RAM.
; Sixteen monotonically decreasing award bytes indexed by result rank. The award renderer adds a flag-dependent bonus and accumulates the selected byte into the driver score.

; Load the awards display and iterate sixteen sorted drivers. Draw their names and a rank-based award, adding a flag-dependent bonus and saving the per-driver award byte. Select one of three one-byte markers from the exact display source, then install the callback and wait.
; Three adjacent tile constants$00,$d6,$d7. The award renderer forms base83ffplus its marker selector and explicitly queues one tile.

; Validate and selectively apply decoded password fields, setting the season sign only on a successful nonempty decode. The score reset entry clears sixteen words; the accumulation entry adds each one-byte award into its driver score with carry.
; Add sixteen one-byte awards into their corresponding little-endian score words, propagating each carry separately.

; Repeated adjacent comparisons sort sixteen driver indices by their unsigned score words, highest first. Build the standings display, render names and scores one row at a time, then either generate the next password or calculate the final-season result and change scene.
; Render the current numeric result and the zero-terminated encoded result string at fixed screen positions before continuing the result-code scene.

; Install the blinking player-name callback and wait for input. A specific four-step held-button sequence clears the winning-driver field. Each input transition restarts matching against the next expected byte.
; Every twenty callbacks toggle the high bit of the stored row coordinate, alternating the player name with the blank string. Mask that bit before drawing.

; Blank tile fields followed by counted composite/display and palette backing for standings/results. Specific internal resource endpoints remain generic where no separate consumed extent is established.
; Marker/count/value RLE stream, exactly 1024 decoded nametable bytes; the following 32-byte palette is independently supplied to the palette copier.
; 32-byte PPU palette copied to the CPU shadow by CopyPaletteFromXY.
; Count byte followed by ten four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X sprite records. Reused at two supplied screen origins.

; Decode the saved password and selectively restore its fields. Preserve the negative season flag only after successful validation, then initialize scroll/motion scratch and the main-menu source pointer.
; Set directional repeat delay and rate before clearing the scene.

; Initialize the menu display, palette, nametable and positioned composite, draw all dependent option fields and install raster and frame callbacks. Set the initial input delay before joining the menu loop.
; Redraw the menu selection, then wait for controller release.
; Rejoin the main-menu input loop after the connected continuation.
; Enter the menu highlight updater; following control continues into the frame timeout test.
; Compare the two-byte frame counter against $4650 and stop audio after that threshold. The connected branch body preserves the original timer comparison and display continuation.
; Reset display, clear scene_state and transfer through the scene dispatcher. Effective bank context ends at that dispatch.
; If repeated directional input is available, preserve its mask and clear the idle timer.

; Update the highlight and wait a frame, then navigate seven choices. Vertical movement wraps 0..6; horizontal movement swaps columns by three while handling choice six specially. Exact button masks come from the shared mask bytes.
; Ignore frames without high-button input. A $20 press calls the menu toggle handler before redisplay.
; Resume the menu refresh path after handling input.
; Clear the idle counter before executing the selected option.
; Enter the RTS-based handler dispatcher. Its bounded seven return-minus-one words are named below; the dispatcher body lies outside this classified span.

; Push a synthetic return address, then the selected handler address minus one. RTS enters the handler and its normal RTS returns through the synthetic continuation. Handlers that pop two bytes deliberately leave this nested menu context.
; Restart menu scene setup after a handler returns.
; Seven little-endian RTS return-minus-one words, indexed by main_menu_cursor 0..6. Adding one yields handler entry; table extent is selector-bounded.
; Discard the current dispatcher return address and jump back to the menu loop.
; When the mode flag is clear, normalize negative track selection to $80 in both selected and active slots. Otherwise call a bank-local helper with a fifteen-unit work value.
; Initialize the sixteen driver indices, show standings, then advance the season flag and preserve it in the saved menu field.
; Calculate the track-dependent numeric field before resuming the menu selection path.
; Choose the active selection from the saved field, forcing zero for a negative season flag. Wait for release and remove one nested return address before returning.
; Stop the audio sequences before entering the connected practice-scene handler.
; Restore the saved selection, reset the display and enter scene 3 with its scene-state byte set to 6.
; Reset display state before opening the connected track-selection screen.
; Enter the connected track-selection screen; the next block supplies the handler continuation.
; For ordinary track indices, blank a bounded RAM text span with tile $DB. Clear the mode flag and copy selected track to active track; negative/special selections skip blanking.
; Initialize scene state; the connected option path follows below.
; Run the three-choice license screen, then save the selected license field before returning.
; Initialize scene state before setup; the connected setup path follows below.
; Run the password/name editor. A successful decode sets the negative season flag before returning.
; Advance a three-state option modulo three and redraw its field. Its precise game setting is unresolved.
; Remove the dispatcher return and resume the main menu loop.
; Toggle the persistent audio option. One branch starts selection zero, the other resets the audio engine; the UI meaning of the bit is not independently established.
; XOR a setting with $15, then redraw its field. This is an encoded two-state setting rather than a numeric increment.
; Discard exactly one disposable JSR return and jump to the menu-loop return continuation. Callers must supply that nested return; this is not an ordinary RTS entry.
; Select sound effect zero and branch into the common effect-request wrapper.
; Select sound effect two, priority one, channel argument one, and tail-call the audio effect requester.

; Select license and track sprite/text pairs through doubled selector indices. The negative season flag forces the special track entry. The following shared entries draw progression and other option labels at fixed positions; each uses its own finite selector domain.
; Select ordinary track0..3 or special track4from the season sign, then draw its sprite and text pointer pair.
; Select one of two fixed text pointers from the mode field and draw it at the shared menu position.
; Negative season mode forces the first description; ordinary mode uses the progression selector to resolve its pointer.
; Draw the sixteen-byte editable player name using the fixed attribute style and origin.
; Provide style one or zero to the shared menu attribute updater.

; Look up selection-specific column, row and width, then update attribute runs every two rows. Special track choice four can request alternate feedback; the confirmation continuation redraws and waits four frames.
; Toggle the attribute style after each row, count down the remaining rows, redraw the cursor and wait for the next frame.
; The first entry advances the pseudo-random state. Two raster callbacks alternate CHR selections $3E/$3B and replace the IRQ callback pointer; one also loads scanline $58.

; Menu row/position bytes, finite pointer planes and repeated counted sprite records. Existing main-menu renderers select license/track/progression subresources; retain neighboring mixed backing without inventing additional schema.
; Reset the shared sixteen-bit frame counter used for menu idle timing.

; Save the current license selection, load the display and draw all three alternatives. Accept directional changes with wraparound, restore the saved field on cancel, or animate the chosen item offscreen on confirmation. A scene escape follows the intro state flag.
; Choose one of three sprite composites and draw it twice, separated by $55 pixels. The temporary active flag prevents the callback from changing animation while the composite is built.

; Clear scroll and motion accumulators, then advance horizontal position using callback-produced fixed-point velocity until the raster position reaches $c8. Wait briefly, restore the idle callback and reset display.

; Use held input during normal play and periodically synthesize directional input in attract mode. Cycle cursor animation every fifteen frames, redraw its composite, and accumulate bounded acceleration and animation phase while exit motion is enabled.
; Advance the raster position with fractional carry, set the next IRQ scanline, and apply the scrolling band. The next hook restores the normal scroll and disables that IRQ.

; Three-choice scalar Y positions and offsets, followed by three sprite-pointer words and further numeric backing. Selector bounds are established by the screen loop; unspecified internal fields remain generic.
; 424-byte marker/count/value stream producing exactly one 1024-byte nametable.
; 32-byte PPU palette for the license selection screen.
; License-selection sprite and small numeric backing: repeated signed coordinate/tile/attribute records. The scene-specific identity of each composite remains uncertain.
; Busy-wait until the menu input/event latch clears. Progress requires its asynchronous updater.

; Normalize the season/track selector, reset scene counters and load the track screen assets. Install the track callback, initialize the cursor and field index, and draw the dependent highlights before waiting.
; Wait for latch release and inspect the scene flag; the $F3 case clears the scene before continuing.
; Clear scene/intro flags and dispatch scene 1.
; Wait for the directional nibble to clear, or process the high-button nibble. Toggle the selected track/distance field and play feedback when the mask permits.
; Clamp out-of-range track values to four before clearing the scene.
; Translate track four to the special $80 selector and return; other values remain unchanged.
; Preserve the input mask across a frame wait.
; Play feedback when the active field is the track selector.
; Move a six-position cursor by two with wrap, or toggle its low bit. Field one redirects to distance editing. Ordinary track choices trigger a preview helper before committing selection.
; Store the grid cursor as the selected track and refresh the numeric display.
; Decrease distance with a floor of one or increase it with a ceiling of fifty. Refresh feedback and the distance display after a successful adjustment.
; Select a four-byte field descriptor. Special selector values shift the last three palette entries by $10 and request a palette upload.
; Install a preview descriptor pointer, normalize track five's helper selector and call the preview helper with argument two.
; Undo the $10 palette shift only for selector zero or values at least four. Ordinary selectors 1..3 return without changing the palette.
; Multiply the distance setting by ten into a two-byte number, select digit tile base $F6 and queue three digits at column ten, row twenty-four.
; For ordinary tracks, calculate and draw the derived numeric field; special selector values clear its eight-cell area. Reset the trailing marker tile in both cases.

; Multiply the progression byte by ten, optionally double and divide for the flagged special case, then multiply by a selector-dependent word. Round from the fractional result and separately divide progression by five for the saved field. The exact game unit remains uncertain.
; Four little-endian word multipliers selected by the low two track bits. Used by the shared multi-byte multiplication helper to derive the displayed track field; its exact unit is unresolved.
; Advance a three-frame animation every fifteen calls, draw the selected preview sprite, then service scene input or an automatic timeout. Input interrupts the scene via sentinel $F3.
; Use the low two bits as a four-entry input-mask index and set a two-frame delay. This is a continuation of the installed track callback.
; After frame $015E synthesize a short high-button event; otherwise copy held and repeated controller masks into menu latches. This artificial UI event is game code, distinct from debugger RAM edits.
; Four input masks $08,$04,$02,$01 selected by the random low two bits in attract-mode handling.
; Seven little-endian sprite pointers. The ordinary cursor selects indices0..5; the alternate mode forces the seventh word.
; Five tile bytes rendered at a fixed track-screen position. Encoding is the game tile set, not ASCII.
; Five four-byte records consumed by DrawMenuFieldAttributeRectangle: row count, Y position, tile value and X position. The selector is clamped to four for the special track.
; Request effect one with priority and channel arguments both one.
; 467-byte marker/count/value stream producing exactly 1024 nametable bytes.
; 32-byte PPU palette for the track selection screen.
; Two-byte origin followed by a count and45 four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X records, consumed through the positioned-composite entry.

; Three entries select fixed X/Y dimensions for the shared pattern helper. The arithmetic entry decomposes the source word into a two-bit high selector and two nibbles, combines three local decimal lookup planes, and normalizes carries at ten into three unpacked decimal digits. This is decimal conversion, not cursor motion.
; Read a four-byte descriptor selected by $ba: row count, Y position, tile data and X position. Draw six cells per row, wait once per row, and move down two rows until the descriptor count expires.

; Input clears bit zero of the continuation flags. Otherwise advance a base60 low counter and its high byte. The waiting entry requires the same nonzero transition in two checks separated by the frame counter, waits ten more frames, then returns that input; a changed transition is saved and release is awaited.
; Interleaved unpacked decimal contributions consumed by the local word-to-three-digit helper. Carries normalize the lower two digit accumulators at 10; this is numeric data, not packed BCD.
; Continuation of the decimal contribution lookup planes across a consecutive physical bank boundary. The helper combines nibble/high-selector contributions into three decimal digits.
; Reset display and select the notice assets with the low two season bits. Load the palette and nametable, then wait for a bounded controller-sensitive interval.
; For a nonzero scene flag, clear scene/audio mode state and switch PRG selection one; otherwise wait for release.
